exam.title: WDE Certified Entry-Level Web Developer
exam.study_prerequisites: No formal prerequisite is published. Practice building and validating semantic, responsive, accessible pages across document structure, text and tables, links and media, forms and foundational CSS, ARIA, structured data, storage, geolocation, SVG, and layered accessibility testing. Prefer native semantics and verify the active version before purchase.

objective_coverage.objective_group: Accessibility, Best Practices, and Modern HTML (20%)

review.notes: All 40 WDE-40-01 objectives are mapped through semantic structure, text/list/table markup, links/media/embeds, labelled constrained forms, foundational CSS, native semantics and ARIA, structured data, Web Storage, Geolocation, SVG, performance and layered accessibility testing. Three scenarios, eight labs and 40 original checks are included. The live page's WDE-41-01 practice-test label is recorded as a provider inconsistency rather than silently treated as the active WDE-40-01 code. O'Reilly and Udemy are automation-blocked; no link is missing. No recalled/live item, answer dump or copied course question is used.

findings.title: Forty HTML objectives require concrete examples
findings.evidence: Existing scenarios were short project prompts, without reproducible original pages or browser evidence.
findings.recommendation: Add three complete original pages,54 core and128 browser checks, all 40 expanded answers andexact code/asset hashes; retain eight wider learner labs as proposed.
findings.resolution: Add three complete original pages,54 core and128 browser checks, all 40 expanded answers andexact code/asset hashes; retain eight wider learner labs as proposed.

findings.title: Native validation is a precise and bypassable contract
findings.evidence: Programmatic length assignments, form.submit, empty patterns, numeric coercion andcustom validity have distinct behaviors; overview shorthand can mislead.
findings.recommendation: Teach and test constraints, clear custom error with empty string, distinguish zero/empty andretain server validation; UTF-16 maxlength tested through actual typing.
findings.resolution: Teach and test constraints, clear custom error with empty string, distinguish zero/empty andretain server validation; UTF-16 maxlength tested through actual typing.

findings.title: Form serialization can omit or repeat entries
findings.evidence: Disabled/unnamed/unchecked controls are omitted; repeated names and submitters need explicit treatment.
findings.recommendation: Verify actual GET/POST entries, readonly/disabled/legend behavior and FormData.getAll; explain that construction does not validate.
findings.resolution: Verify actual GET/POST entries, readonly/disabled/legend behavior and FormData.getAll; explain that construction does not validate.

findings.title: HTML containers are not all landmarks
findings.evidence: Article is not a landmark andsection/form need names; header/footer depend on context. ARIA does not add behavior or remove focus.
findings.recommendation: Correct landmark teaching and all relevant answers; inspect actual AX names and keyboard operation with native controls.
findings.resolution: Correct landmark teaching and all relevant answers; inspect actual AX names and keyboard operation with native controls.

findings.title: Unsupported-element fallback differs from failed-source behavior
findings.evidence: Video child fallback is not automatically shown when all sources fail; Boolean attributes depend on presence and preload is only a hint.
findings.recommendation: Provide outside-player transcript/download links; actually decode original silent clip and parse caption, while qualifying unsupported/cross-browser limits.
findings.resolution: Provide outside-player transcript/download links; actually decode original silent clip and parse caption, while qualifying unsupported/cross-browser limits.

findings.title: Storage access and location require usable fallback paths
findings.evidence: Storage getters and writes can fail; invalid values and unrelated keys must be handled; location can fail or be unavailable.
findings.recommendation: Add validated preferences, key-scopedforget andexplicit exception paths; exercise eleven fake-provider cases without actual location/permission changes.
findings.resolution: Add validated preferences, key-scopedforget andexplicit exception paths; exercise eleven fake-provider cases without actual location/permission changes.

findings.evidence: Credential TestNow conflicts with homepage Pearson/OnVUE; practice-row 41-01 differs from active 40-01 and duration/proctoring prose is ambiguous.

    rows.append(row);print(name,row['status'],row.get('result',{}).get('messages',[]))
    (o/'markup-checks.json').write_text(json.dumps(rows,indent=2,ensure_ascii=False)+'\n',encoding='utf-8')

groups.title: Block 1: HTML Fundamentals — 6 items, 15%
objectives: 1.1 Build a standards-mode HTML document with doctype, language, head metadata, title, and body.
1.2 Distinguish the default behavior and appropriate use of block and inline elements.
1.3 Encode reserved characters with entities and use non-breaking spaces only where meaningful.
1.4 Declare UTF-8 and keep document, editor, and server encodings consistent.
1.5 Write useful HTML comments without exposing private information.
1.6 Apply html, head, title, and body correctly and validate the resulting skeleton.

groups.title: Block 2: Text Formatting and Structure — 8 items, 20%
objectives: 2.1 Use strong, em, u, del, sup, sub, and mark according to meaning rather than appearance.
2.2 Build a logical heading hierarchy that supports navigation and accessibility.
2.3 Structure prose with paragraphs and control visual spacing with CSS.
2.4 Use br for meaningful line breaks and hr for thematic changes.
2.5 Mark block and inline quotations, works, and abbreviations with appropriate elements.
2.6 Mark code, preserved text, user input, and program output with code, pre, kbd, and samp.
2.7 Choose and nest ordered, unordered, and description lists correctly.
2.8 Construct data tables with captions, row groups, header cells, scope, and sparing cell spans.

groups.title: Block 3: Multimedia and Hyperlinks — 8 items, 20%
objectives: 3.1 Embed responsive images with appropriate alternative text, intrinsic size, srcset, and sizes.
3.2 Create descriptive internal, external, fragment, email, telephone, and download links; secure new-window links.
3.3 Embed accessible audio and video with controls, sources, captions, posters, and appropriate playback behavior.
3.4 Create image maps while preserving keyboard access and equivalent text alternatives.
3.5 Associate self-contained media and captions with figure and figcaption.
3.6 Embed external content with titled, responsive iframes and appropriate sandbox/referrer controls.
3.7 Turn media into links while preserving destination meaning, focus visibility, and target size.
3.8 Declare and test favicons in suitable formats and sizes.

groups.title: Block 4: Forms and Styling — 10 items, 25%
objectives: 4.1 Choose suitable form controls and input types; connect labels and stable names/IDs.
4.2 Select GET for safe retrieval and POST for state changes; configure action, encoding, and autocomplete.
4.3 Group related inputs with fieldset and legend; distinguish value, placeholder, disabled, and readonly.
4.4 Apply native constraints such as required, min/max, maxlength, pattern, and step and provide useful errors.
4.5 Build labelled select controls and group options when needed.
4.6 Apply inline and internal CSS while recognizing that external stylesheets normally scale better.
4.7 Use classes for reusable styling and IDs for unique identifiers/anchors rather than high-specificity styling.
4.8 Establish readable color and typography with adequate contrast.
4.9 Use span and div only when a more meaningful semantic element does not fit.
4.10 Reason about content, padding, border, margin, and border-box sizing.

groups.title: Block 5: Accessibility, Best Practices, and Modern HTML — 8 items, 20%
objectives: 5.1 Apply the perceivable, operable, understandable, and robust accessibility principles.
5.2 Use native semantics first and add accurate ARIA roles, states, and properties only when needed.
5.3 Structure landmarks with header, nav, main, article, section, aside, and footer.
5.4 Annotate structured data with microdata/Schema.org and recognize microformat use cases.
5.5 Use Geolocation with permission/error handling and Web Storage with privacy/quota awareness.
5.6 Embed accessible, scalable SVG and reuse symbols where appropriate.
5.7 Produce readable, minimal, semantic markup and reduce avoidable loading cost.
5.8 Combine automated checks with keyboard and screen-reader spot checks.
